[[Houston, Texas]], [[United States|USA]] | awards = [[NABC Defensive Player of the Year]] (2008) [[Big East Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big East Player of the Year]] (with [[DeJuan Blair]]) (2009) }} '''Hasheem Thabeet''' (born '''Hashim Thabit Manka''' on February 16, 1987 in [[Dar es Salaam]], [[Tanzania]]{{cite web|url=http://www.uconnhuskies.com/sports/MBasketball/2007/Bios/Thabeet.html|title=Hasheem Thabeet profile|accessdate=2009-01-25}}) is a [[Tanzania]]n [[college basketball]] player for the [[Connecticut Huskies men's basketball|UConn Huskies]] in the [[United States|USA]]. At 7'3" and 263 lbs, Thabeet is the tallest player ever to play for the Huskies.{{cite web|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2006/sioncampus/07/18/uconn.hasheem/index.html|title=Biggest Man on Campus - Tanzanian freshman tallest ever at UConn|date=Tuesday July 18, 2006|accessdate=2009-01-25}} He did not begin to play basketball until the age of 15, when he began to watch pickup games in Tanzania.{{cite web|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2006/sioncampus/07/18/uconn.hasheem/index.html|title=Biggest Man on Campus - Tanzanian freshman tallest ever at UConn|date=Tuesday July 18, 2006|accessdate=2009-02-11}} Thabeet is projected to be a first round selection in the [[2009 NBA Draft]] after deciding to forgo his final year of eligibility. == Early career in Tanzania == Thabeet began playing basketball when he was in Makongo secondary school in Dar es salaam Tanzania. He was not interested in playing, but when he attended once in a street basketball practice, one player was amazed by his height and offered him sports shoes and invited him to come to play the next day. As a member of his school basketball team, he was selected to compete in the East African Games in [[Nairobi, Kenya]] where an agent saw him and offered him a basketball scholarship in the United States. In Tanzania, people where surprised when he was walking in the streets. After Thabeet's father died, Thabeet removed his last name and took his middle name as his last. Before attending [[Connecticut Huskies|UConn]], Hasheem attended the [[Cypress Christian School]] in [[Houston, Texas]], where he averaged 16 points, 10 rebounds and four blocks per game. == University of Connecticut == ===2006–2007=== As a freshman, he averaged 6.2 points and 3.8 blocks per game.[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/player/profile?playerId=31559 ESPN - Hasheem Thabeet Stats] On December 3, 2006, Thabeet tied a UConn record with 10 [[Block (basketball)|blocks]].[http://www.msnbc.msn.com/id/16025260/ Thabeet’s record 10 blocks key UConn’s big win - College basketball - MSNBC.com] Thabeet was named to the 2007 All-[[Big East]] Rookie Team, along with fellow teammate [[Jerome Dyson]]. ===2007–2008=== As a sophomore he saw increased minutes and he averaged 10.5 points, 7.9 rebounds, 4.5 blocks on the season. On January 5, 2008, he tied his career high in blocks with 10 in the Huskies' 73-67 loss at [[University of Notre Dame]].[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=280050087 ESPN - Connecticut vs. Notre Dame - Recap - January 05, 2008] Thabeet was named Big East Defensive Player of the Year and to the Second Team All [[Big East]] ===2008–2009=== As a junior at UConn, Thabeet emerged on the national scene, averaging 13.6 points and 10.8 rebounds. He earned his first career [[triple-double]] against [[Providence College]] on January 31, 2009, with 15 points, 11 rebounds and 10 blocks.[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/boxscore?gameId=290310041 Providence vs. Connecticut Box Score] He finished with 152 blocks on the season, and he is known for the shots he prevents from ever being taken. He was named [[Big East]] Defensive Player of the Year and was co-[[Big East Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big East Player of the Year]] with [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pitt]]'s [[DeJuan Blair]].[http://www.bigeast.org/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=99617&DB_OEM_ID=19400&ATCLID=3689664&SPID=11228 Thabeet, Blair Share BIG EAST Player of the Year Award] He was named Second Team All-America and National Defensive Player of the Year. Thabeet surpassed the 1,000 point mark against Purdue on March 26, 2009. He was the 3rd UConn player that season to do so (Jerome Dyson and [[AJ Price]] were the others). Thabeet helped lead UConn to their first [[Final Four]] appearance since 2004. Thabeet decided to forgo his senior season and declare for the [[2009 NBA Draft]] on April 14th, 2009. He has the chance of being one of the top three picks in the NBA Draft. He is projected to go third which is currently held by the third pick, the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] (As of June 18th), after Blake Griffin of Oklahoma, and James Harden of Arizona State. == Personal == Thabeet is the son of Thabit Manka and Rukia Manka. His mother, Rukia, resides in Dar es Salaam. He has one sister, Sham, and one brother, Ahkbar. On June 15, 2009, he stated on the show "Jim Rome Is Burning" that he is a Muslim.
